Subject: Capacity uplift and term extension — Q1 spike

Hi Marcus —

Quick context: we saw a ~65% week-over-week spike in token consumption for our triage + summarization pipelines across April (attached). That pushed us well above our committed monthly run-rate and the elastic bursts burned through the short-term allotment. Our CTO wants a proposal that lets us:

- Smooth unit economics across the next three quarters
- Add capacity in a staged way (we can't take the full uplift at once)
- Preserve predictability (prefer some committed capacity + burst credits)

Can your team put together a phased renewal proposal (pricing + SLA implications) and an ops checklist for rolling the capacity up with minimal latency regressions? We can sign quickly if the numbers make sense — procurement is on-copy.

Thanks for the note, Sanjay — and thanks for the usage CSV. Looping in Priyom (sales) and Soojin (CS/ops) so we can coordinate a phased commercial + operational plan. Quick take from my side after a first pass on the numbers:

- April spike looks concentrated to two endpoints (triage + summarization), which aligns with the model mix shift you mentioned on last sync.
- If you want smoothing, a 2-stage uplift (20% immediate committed + 10% ramp next quarter) generally provides the best short-term unit cost improvement while limiting capex/commitment risk.
- We can layer burst credits for traffic spikes and a short-term rate cap to reduce unpredictability.

Priyom — can you draft a phased commercial with an estimated per-token blended rate for each phase? Soojin — can you add ops notes about model-mix and caching to avoid latency regressions during the ramp?

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through a concrete proposal. Attaching our initial analysis and a first-draft phased proposal for you to review.

Attachments: redwood-q1-usage-analysis.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB); redwood-phased-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Hi Sanjay / Marcus —

Thanks for the details; below is a concise phased commercial we can move forward with if it maps to your internal goals. This is an initial offer (proposal_BR-2027-0043.pdf attached) — happy to tweak.

Summary (three-phase approach):

Phase 1 — Immediate smoothing (quarter 1 of renewal):
- Committed uplift: +20% of current committed TUs (tokens)
- Duration: 3 months (Q3 planning window)
- Effective blended price: $0.00080 / token (estimated, blended across model mix)
- Included: 5M burst credit bucket for unexpected spikes

Phase 2 — Controlled ramp (next quarter):
- Additional +10% committed uplift (so total +30%)
- Duration: 3 months
- Unit price steps down to $0.00074 / token for volume above Phase 1 baseline

Phase 3 — Term extension and volume discount:
- Option to extend term +12 months at an 8% discount vs Phase 2 blended rates
- Annualized cost predictability with quarterly true-ups

Estimated savings vs current elastic-only spend: ~22% in Year 1 assuming burst credits and conservative usage profile.

Commercial logistics / next steps:
- If accepted, we can send a DocuSign link for the phased addendum (see placeholder below).
- Deal id: BR-2027-0043 (tracking in our CRM).
- Timeline: sign within 72 hours for Q3 effective uplift (we'll prioritize capacity reservations).

Subject: Re: Capacity uplift and term extension — ops considerations

Thanks team — adding the operational checklist and risk mitigation recommendations so the uplift is low-friction from an SLO perspective. High-level ops notes: 

1) Model mix and token mix
- Move high-frequency, short-context calls (triage) to a smaller, cheaper model variant where acceptable — ~12% cost reduction expected for those calls.
- Keep summarization on higher-capacity model but add prefix caching for repeated sections.

2) Batching & caching knobs
- Increase batching window for bulk summarization jobs (non-latency-sensitive) to 50ms for 2–3x throughput gains.
- Enable KV cache sharing for sessioned flows to reduce repeated compute.

3) SLA impact and Dedicated option
- For predictable throughput at scale, Dedicated capacity reduces 99th percentile latency variance; recommend evaluating a dedicated pool if you intend to keep >60% committed utilization long-term.
- If you go phased commit + bursts, we can include an ops addendum to guarantee ramp timelines and provide a temporary SLA credit if latency regresses during the first 30 days.

4) Rollout plan (recommended)
- Week 0: sign addendum + reserve capacity
- Week 1–2: model-mix rollout to 15% of traffic (monitor token mix / latency)
- Week 3–6: increase committed routing to Phase 1 target, enable caching
- Week 8+: evaluate Phase 2 uplift; lock in dedicated options if utilization stays high

Attachment: ops-sla-addendum.docx (DOCX, 28KB) — includes fallback policy language and a short checklist for pull-through testing.

If you'd like, Marcus/ Priyom and I can host a 30-minute operational deep-dive tomorrow to walk the rollout steps and confirm monitoring dashboards to share with your on-call.

— Soojin
